hero.headline: Martin County deputies rescue man attempting suicide in ocean
hero.teaser:
Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies pulled a distressed man from the ocean Monday after he swam out with no intention of returning, according to the agency.

The Martin County
hero.body:
Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies pulled a distressed man from the ocean Monday after he swam out with no intention of returning, according to the agency.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office responded to a call about a man who said he was going to swim into the ocean without intending to return. Marine deputies, the aviation unit, and a Martin County lifeguard located the man in the water and jumped in to stop him from continuing.

Video from the Martin County Sheriff's Office shows several deputies surrounding the man in the water during the rescue. The agency said the responders quickly realized the situation and acted to prevent the man from continuing.

The man was pulled from the water and is now receiving help, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested on attempted murder charge after firing bullet through bathroom door
cards.teaser: A 23-year-old Fort Pierce man faces attempted felony murder and kidnapping charges after firing a gun through a bathroom door during a domestic disturbance Sunday.
cards.body:
Daniel Hsu, 23, from Fort Pierce, was arrested Sunday and faces charges of attempted felony murder, kidnapping, tampering with a witness, simple battery and grand theft of a motor vehicle. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office and Fort Pierce Police Department conducted an extensive search for Hsu near Porpoise Beach on Hutchinson Island following the incident.

Deputies responded to a residence on the 1700 block of Wyoming Avenue around 11:30 a.m. Sunday regarding a domestic disturbance. Hsu became involved in a verbal argument with the victim, which led the victim to lock herself inside a bathroom. Hsu fired a bullet through the bathroom door and then left the residence in a vehicle, according to the sheriff's office.

Fort Pierce Police Department officers located the vehicle near Porpoise Beach. At 2:30 p.m., Hsu's family located him and alerted a passing Fort Pierce Police Department officer. Hsu was taken into custody and his firearm was retrieved. Hsu remains in the St. Lucie County Jail on no bond.

cards.headline: More than 50 St. Lucie County residents targeted in law enforcement impersonation scam
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office received more than 50 reports from people targeted by a scam involving callers impersonating law enforcement officers. Scammers have been usin
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office received more than 50 reports from people targeted by a scam involving callers impersonating law enforcement officers. Scammers have been using the names of the Civil Judicial Services Bureau, Lt. Michael O'Brien and retired Sgt. Jeff Buchanan when making fraudulent calls, according to the sheriff's office.

Deputies said the scam follows a repeated pattern. A caller claims the victim missed court or jury duty and that there is a warrant for their arrest. The sheriff's office warned that scammers may use official-sounding language and personal information to make the call appear legitimate.

The sheriff's office said scammers use fear, urgency and threats of arrest to pressure victims into taking immediate action. Deputies said residents who receive one of these calls should hang up and not provide personal or financial information. Victims should not send money or make any payments and should not trust the caller ID or the name provided by the caller.

If residents have questions about a legitimate court matter, they should contact the appropriate agency using a verified phone number, according to the sheriff's office.

cards.headline: Florida emergency management chief Kevin Guthrie joins Jay Collins gubernatorial ticket hours before primary
cards.teaser: Jay Collins has chosen Florida Division of Emergency Management Director Kevin Guthrie as his running mate in the Republican race for governor, announcing the pick just hours before Tuesday's primary.
cards.body:
Collins announced the pick as he tries to close a significant polling gap with frontrunner Byron Donalds, who has held a commanding lead in many polls. Collins said he spent weeks considering who could serve as his second-in-command and wanted competence, leadership, character and someone who could step in and lead on day one, rather than someone chosen for demographic or geographic reasons.

Guthrie is still leading the Florida Division of Emergency Management during hurricane season. Asked whether he would have to resign, Guthrie said he had not yet spoken with Gov. Ron DeSantis and that conversation would happen Tuesday. If required to resign, Guthrie said he will do so and focus fully on the campaign, and his second-in-command, Ben Fairbrother, is prepared to take over the agency if necessary.

Guthrie said he has spent nearly 37 years in public safety, including more than two decades with the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office, before moving into emergency management. He eventually became director of the state's emergency management agency under DeSantis. Guthrie called DeSantis the best governor he has worked for and said the governor had empowered him throughout his career. Collins said he wants the lieutenant governor to have a more active role than a traditional ceremonial position, focusing on safety, security, readiness, and response.

cards.headline: Vero Beach woman shot dead in roadway; Indian River County authorities search for Sebastian man nationwide
cards.teaser: A 52-year-old woman died Sunday morning after being shot in the roadway in the 500 block of 1st Street in Vero Beach, and the Indian River County Sheriff's Offi.
cards.body:
A 52-year-old woman died Sunday morning after being shot in the roadway in the 500 block of 1st Street in Vero Beach, and the Indian River County Sheriff's Office is searching nationwide for 33-year-old Matthew Allen Waggle of Sebastian as a person of interest in what investigators are treating as a domestic violence homicide.

The sheriff's office received a 911 call at approximately 8:41 a.m. Sunday reporting a woman in the roadway. Deputies found the woman with an apparent gunshot wound and began life-saving measures. She was transported to a trauma center, where she was later pronounced dead. Detectives and crime scene personnel processed the scene outside the victim's home.

Sheriff Eric Flowers said investigators believe Waggle and the victim were in an on-and-off relationship and that he fled the area in a vehicle. Authorities have issued a nationwide be on the lookout for Waggle, who should be considered armed and dangerous. Marco Cardenas, a longtime resident of the area whose siblings live in the complex, said his brother heard the shot. Cardenas said the neighborhood is typically quiet.

Flowers said detectives are using resources such as flock cameras to investigate Waggle's whereabouts. State Rep. Debra Tendrich, who sponsored House Bill 277 to strengthen protections for domestic violence survivors, said domestic violence is not contained in a specific area and that tracking someone across state lines is very difficult. The bill, signed into law by Gov. Ron DeSantis in July, adds victim relocation allowance, protection for military families and pets, and stronger protections for victims. Anyone with information is asked to contact Det. Kachele at 772-978-6240 or mkachele@ircsheriff.org, or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

cards.headline: Home insurance premiums drop in Indian River County in first half of 2026
cards.teaser: Indian River County saw the largest decrease in average home insurance premiums among Treasure Coast counties in the first six months of 2026.
cards.body:
Average home insurance premiums in Indian River County fell from $4,453 in January 2026 to $4,334 in July 2026, a decrease of 2.7 percent, according to the July 2026 Property Insurance Stability Report from Florida's Insurance Commissioner. The decrease was the largest among Treasure Coast counties.

Martin County saw average premiums drop from $5,993 to $5,899, a decrease of 1.6 percent, while St. Lucie County saw premiums fall from $3,522 to $3,491, a decrease of 0.9 percent. The report showed decreasing property insurance premiums in 51 of 67 Florida counties.

The report cited reduced litigation from state reforms as one of the main drivers in lowering rates for many insurers. Palm Beach County Commissioner Gregg Weiss, who dropped wind coverage on his West Palm Beach home several years ago, said dropping insurance coverage carries risks, especially if a damaging storm hits, and is an option available only to homeowners who don't have a mortgage.

cards.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
cards.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
cards.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

The Mets are off Monday before returning home Tuesday to begin a six-game series against the Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. First pitch for Tuesday's opener is scheduled for 6:10 p.m.

hero.headline: Martin County deputies rescue man attempting suicide in ocean
hero.teaser:
Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies pulled a distressed man from the ocean Monday after he swam out with no intention of returning, according to the agency.

The Martin County
hero.body:
Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies pulled a distressed man from the ocean Monday after he swam out with no intention of returning, according to the agency.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office responded to a call about a man who said he was going to swim into the ocean without intending to return. Marine deputies, the aviation unit, and a Martin County lifeguard located the man in the water and jumped in to stop him from continuing.

Video from the Martin County Sheriff's Office shows several deputies surrounding the man in the water during the rescue. The agency said the responders quickly realized the situation and acted to prevent the man from continuing.

The man was pulled from the water and is now receiving help, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office.

cards.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
cards.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
cards.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

The Mets are off Monday before returning home Tuesday to begin a six-game series against the Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. First pitch for Tuesday's opener is scheduled for 6:10 p.m.

hero.headline: More than 50 St. Lucie County residents targeted in law enforcement impersonation scam
hero.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office received more than 50 reports from people targeted by a scam involving callers impersonating law enforcement officers. Scammers have been usin
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office received more than 50 reports from people targeted by a scam involving callers impersonating law enforcement officers. Scammers have been using the names of the Civil Judicial Services Bureau, Lt. Michael O'Brien and retired Sgt. Jeff Buchanan when making fraudulent calls, according to the sheriff's office.

 Deputies said the scam follows a repeated pattern. A caller claims the victim missed court or jury duty and that there is a warrant for their arrest. The sheriff's office warned that scammers may use official-sounding language and personal information to make the call appear legitimate.

 The sheriff's office said scammers use fear, urgency and threats of arrest to pressure victims into taking immediate action. Deputies said residents who receive one of these calls should hang up and not provide personal or financial information. Victims should not send money or make any payments and should not trust the caller ID or the name provided by the caller.

 If residents have questions about a legitimate court matter, they should contact the appropriate agency using a verified phone number, according to the sheriff's office.

hero.headline: Home insurance premiums drop in Indian River County in first half of 2026
hero.teaser: Indian River County saw the largest decrease in average home insurance premiums among Treasure Coast counties in the first six months of 2026.
hero.body:
Average home insurance premiums in Indian River County fell from $4,453 in January 2026 to $4,334 in July 2026, a decrease of 2.7 percent, according to the July 2026 Property Insurance Stability Report from Florida's Insurance Commissioner. The decrease was the largest among Treasure Coast counties.

Martin County saw average premiums drop from $5,993 to $5,899, a decrease of 1.6 percent, while St. Lucie County saw premiums fall from $3,522 to $3,491, a decrease of 0.9 percent. The report showed decreasing property insurance premiums in 51 of 67 Florida counties.

The report cited reduced litigation from state reforms as one of the main drivers in lowering rates for many insurers. Palm Beach County Commissioner Gregg Weiss, who dropped wind coverage on his West Palm Beach home several years ago, said dropping insurance coverage carries risks, especially if a damaging storm hits, and is an option available only to homeowners who don't have a mortgage.

cards.headline: Vero Beach woman shot dead in roadway; Indian River County authorities search for Sebastian man nationwide
cards.teaser: A 52-year-old woman died Sunday morning after being shot in the roadway in the 500 block of 1st Street in Vero Beach, and the Indian River County Sheriff's Offi.
cards.body:
A 52-year-old woman died Sunday morning after being shot in the roadway in the 500 block of 1st Street in Vero Beach, and the Indian River County Sheriff's Office is searching nationwide for 33-year-old Matthew Allen Waggle of Sebastian as a person of interest in what investigators are treating as a domestic violence homicide.

The sheriff's office received a 911 call at approximately 8:41 a.m. Sunday reporting a woman in the roadway. Deputies found the woman with an apparent gunshot wound and began life-saving measures. She was transported to a trauma center, where she was later pronounced dead. Detectives and crime scene personnel processed the scene outside the victim's home.

Sheriff Eric Flowers said investigators believe Waggle and the victim were in an on-and-off relationship and that he fled the area in a vehicle. Authorities have issued a nationwide be on the lookout for Waggle, who should be considered armed and dangerous. Marco Cardenas, a longtime resident of the area whose siblings live in the complex, said his brother heard the shot. Cardenas said the neighborhood is typically quiet.

Flowers said detectives are using resources such as flock cameras to investigate Waggle's whereabouts. State Rep. Debra Tendrich, who sponsored House Bill 277 to strengthen protections for domestic violence survivors, said domestic violence is not contained in a specific area and that tracking someone across state lines is very difficult. The bill, signed into law by Gov. Ron DeSantis in July, adds victim relocation allowance, protection for military families and pets, and stronger protections for victims. Anyone with information is asked to contact Det. Kachele at 772-978-6240 or mkachele@ircsheriff.org, or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.
